brief:
We are naming a UK company: an AI consulting and products agency for mid-market and enterprise
buyers (CFOs, CISOs, operations leads). Its thesis is an architecture of distrust: AI agents hold
only the capabilities they are given, risky actions wait for human approval, and information flows
only where it may. It aims to be worth £100m, so the name must be sober and weighty, memorable, a
little wry but never silly (think Palantir, Anduril, Thought Machine, Darktrace, Tailscale). Plain
English single words are all taken; coined words, literary or historical borrowings, short phrases
and a "Labs" suffix are fine. It must not clash with a known AI or security company.

candidates.name: Cordon
candidates.pitch: A cordon lets movement through only at sanctioned points—AI actions cross only when a human waves them on.

candidates.name: Gnomon
candidates.pitch: An architectural term for precision and oversight, offering the sobriety and weight required for enterprise buyers.

candidates.name: Certes
candidates.pitch: Medieval certainty; archaic gravitas suggesting verified, trustworthy AI action under human sanction.

candidates.name: Hadrian Labs
candidates.pitch: Evokes the Roman boundary wall, signaling strict limits and a controlled architecture of distrust.

candidates.name: Billet Labs
candidates.pitch: Military quarters assigned strictly by warrant, capturing constrained agency, compartmentalized access, and disciplined, no-nonsense UK engineering.

candidates.name: AegisVector
candidates.pitch: Aegis implies protection, vector signals directionality; together they convey AI that moves only where authorised.

candidates.name: NovaPulse AI Solutions
candidates.pitch: A modern, innovative name that conveys energy and cutting-edge AI solutions for business.

candidates.name: Aegis
candidates.pitch: Classical shield; connotes protection through careful permission-gating and bounded agent autonomy.

candidates.name: Sovereign Air
candidates.pitch: Evoking 'air gaps' and supreme authority, it signals absolute operational boundaries, strict oversight, and elite British enterprise gravitas.

candidates.name: Sentinel
candidates.pitch: Watchful guardian; evokes controlled oversight and the architecture of distrust at your core.

candidates.name: Cautia
candidates.pitch: Derived from “cautious”, a concise coined word evoking measured AI trust, fitting mid‑market enterprise seriousness.

candidates.name: Veto Labs
candidates.pitch: A wry nod to the human-in-the-loop, ensuring risky AI actions require explicit human approval.

candidates.name: Corbel
candidates.pitch: An architectural stone bracket supporting massive weight only through structural restraint, embodying an unyielding, deliberate architecture of distrust.

candidates.name: Vouchsafe Labs
candidates.pitch: A deliberately old-fashioned promise of permission and protection, capturing governed AI that earns trust rather than assuming it.

candidates.name: Countermand Labs
candidates.pitch: Countermand means revoking an order, capturing the human power to stop risky AI actions before they proceed.

candidates.name: Imprimatur Labs
candidates.pitch: Imprimatur means official approval, fitting a firm where risky AI actions wait for human sign-off.

candidates.name: Seneschal
candidates.pitch: A seneschal held a lord's keys but never his throne—our agents act only with delegated, revocable authority.

candidates.name: Redoubt
candidates.pitch: A fortified refuge with clear defensive boundaries, evoking agents contained by design and consequential actions held behind approval.

candidates.name: Auctra
candidates.pitch: A coined blend of authority and strata, suggesting carefully layered powers, controls, and accountability for enterprise AI.

candidates.name: VeritasGate Labs
candidates.pitch: Latin for truth gate, signalling controlled AI flow and human‑approved decisions, a sober, weighty brand.

candidates.name: Chancery
candidates.pitch: Like a chancery court, every sensitive action is sealed, recorded, and released only once duly authorised.

candidates.name: Bailiwick Labs
candidates.pitch: Bailiwick means one's rightful domain, fitting AI agents confined to approved capabilities and information boundaries.

candidates.name: Penstock Labs
candidates.pitch: The sluice-gate that meters a river — Penstock fits an architecture admitting capability and information only where, and when, they should.

candidates.name: Claustra Labs
candidates.pitch: Latin for barred gates and grates—the physical architecture of 'information flows only where it may,' rendered sober and weighty.

candidates.name: Runnymede Labs
candidates.pitch: At Runnymede, power accepted limits; AI agents should act only within granted boundaries.

candidates.name: Chary Labs
candidates.pitch: Chary means cautiously reluctant—exactly the posture of least-privilege agents, mandatory approval gates, and need-to-know data flows.

candidates.name: Anchorite Labs
candidates.pitch: The medieval anchorite was walled into a cell by choice — wry, weighty shorthand for capability held strictly to its granted bounds.

candidates.name: Barbican
candidates.pitch: A medieval fortress guarding the gates — fitting for a firm channelling AI capability and data only where they should flow.

candidates.name: Seneschal Labs
candidates.pitch: A seneschal stewards power under strict instruction; our agents act only when explicitly granted.

candidates.name: Provost Labs
candidates.pitch: A provost governs by consent and check; AI agents should hold only delegated authority.

candidates.name: Vallum Labs
candidates.pitch: The Roman frontier system: ramparts, ditches, and controlled gates enforcing sovereign boundaries—architecture of distrust made imperial infrastructure.
